entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: State your business on this track, citizen.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: The watch is set. Speak from where you stand.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: The book has this. Stand there while I check it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Back again, citizen.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: The column pitched four tents on a flat shelf up in the hills, over the Mile House track. We have a tarn fed by a spring at our backs. The Gideon road cannot see the camp.

variants.low: Four tents on a flat shelf over the Mile House track. A tarn lies behind them. Nothing more.
variants.high: Four tents sit on a flat shelf over the Mile House track, with a spring tarn behind them. Fill your flask there, citizen. The water is clean.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: I set the watch. It is called on the hour, day and night. The men at the barricade take a levy from each traveller. That money buys what we eat.

variants.low: Watch on the hour. The barricade takes a levy from all. It buys our food.
variants.high: I set the watch, called on the hour, day and night. The barricade takes a levy from each traveller for our food. Pay it plain and you will have no trouble from me.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Six names stand on the roster: mine, then five heirs of the column. Their grandfathers were drawn from every province. The colours came down to them from their fathers. Each one stands a watch.

variants.low: Six on the roster. Me, then five heirs of the column. Each stands a watch.
variants.high: Six names are on the roster: mine, then five heirs of the column. Their grandfathers were drawn from every province. The colours came down to them from their fathers. Each one stands a watch. I am proud of that.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Up the hill above the tents the hackwings have their nests. Stay on the path under the bench and they keep to their rocks. After dark, the rats get into the meal sacks. We hang what we can.

variants.low: Hackwings up the hill. Rats at night. Keep to the path.
variants.high: Up the hill above the tents the hackwings have their nests. Stay on the path under the bench. After dark, the rats get into the meal sacks, so hang your food from the pole by my tent.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Take the track down from the barricade. It brings you to the Eagle's Mile House, then farther to Cartwright's Cross. You will find both on the Gideon road. Past the Cross the Blackwood Road climbs west. I have never walked it.

variants.low: Down the track from the barricade. Mile House, then Cartwright's Cross. The Gideon road is there.
variants.high: Take the track down from the barricade. It brings you to the Eagle's Mile House, then farther to Cartwright's Cross. You will find both on the Gideon road. Past the Cross the Blackwood Road climbs west. I have never walked it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: I keep the watch for the column. I write the roster in my own hand. The pay book is in my tent, with the column's last entry in it. A stranger gets my questions first. I hear his business before anyone draws.

variants.low: I keep the watch. I write the roster. The pay book holds the last entry. A stranger answers me before blades come out.
variants.high: I keep the watch for the column. I write the roster in my own hand. The pay book holds the column's last entry. A stranger speaks with me before any blade is drawn. Speak plainly, citizen. It goes well.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Some garrisons stayed behind in the province once the Empire pulled out. Their heirs are counted as Legion too. The old road stages are Legion work. Salvage families keep a few of them today.

variants.low: Garrisons stayed behind once the Empire pulled out. Heirs are Legion too. The stages are Legion work. Salvage families keep a few.
variants.high: Some garrisons stayed behind in the province once the Empire pulled out. Their heirs are Legion too, as my men are. The old road stages are Legion work. Salvage families keep a few of them today.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Levy at the barricade.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Relieved. Mark the roster.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: State your business, traveller. Levy first.

variants.low: Levy first, traveller.
variants.high: Welcome, traveller. Levy, then your business.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Barricade's closed till the morning watch.

variants.low: Closed till morning.
variants.high: Closed till morning watch, traveller. Try at light.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Serjeant, here is the one the book names.

variants.low: Hold. Serjeant!
variants.high: Hold, you! Serjeant, turn out the watch! Give yourself up.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: You paid in full before. I know the face.

variants.low: Paid before. On with you.
variants.high: Paid in full last time. The fire's open.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: We're four tents on a bench, a flat shelf of hill with the Mile House track running below it. There's a spring pool behind us. I'm Severa Maro. I go down to the barricade to ask each traveller for the levy of passage. That's the Legion's name for it, so I use it.

variants.low: Four tents on a bench over the Mile House track. Pay the levy of passage at the barricade.
variants.high: We're four tents on a bench over the Mile House track, with a spring pool at our backs. I'm Severa Maro. Stop at the barricade, pay the levy of passage and I'll point you to the fire. The cook has a pot on most days.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: I step out at the barricade and ask for the levy of passage, as the book words it. Until the pot has fed you, you're a traveller to us. Your coin goes to the cook fire. It's thin work, I'll say that. The pot gets thinner each month.

variants.low: I ask for the levy at the barricade. You're a traveller until you've been fed. The coin goes to the pot.
variants.high: I step out at the barricade and ask for the levy of passage, as the book words it. You're a traveller to us until you've eaten. Pay it and the cook fire will have a bowl for you, thin as it is.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Six on the roster. The serjeant is Gnaeus Martius. The other five of us had grandfathers from different provinces. He writes every name in his own hand. He won't strike one while the man lives.

variants.low: Six on the roster. Gnaeus Martius, the serjeant, keeps it. Ask him about the rest of us.
variants.high: Six on the roster. The serjeant is Gnaeus Martius. The other five of us had grandfathers from different provinces. He writes every name in his own hand. I eat from the same pot as the rest each evening.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Rats in the meal sacks, hackwings on the hill above. I'd sooner lose a day to the hackwings. They don't eat what the levy bought.

variants.low: Rats at night, hackwings on the hill. Keep off the slope.
variants.high: Rats in the meal sacks, hackwings on the hill above. Don't climb the slope behind the tents. The hackwings don't care for visitors. I'd sooner not carry you down.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Go down the track from the barricade and the Mile House comes first, the one called of the Eagle. Cartwright's Cross comes after it. Both lie along the Gideon road, so either one sets you toward the city. Settle the levy before you start down. I'd sooner take it face to face than chase you.

variants.low: Down the track. Mile House first, then Cartwright's Cross, both on the Gideon road. Levy first.
variants.high: Go down the track from the barricade and the Mile House comes first, the one called of the Eagle. Cartwright's Cross comes after it. Both are on the Gideon road. Mind the steep ground below us.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: The column was Legion soldiers set to hold the border road. The order to leave came about two centuries back. The column's last entry is still in our pay book. We're what the book still counts. Call the levy a robbery and I'll answer you sharply.

variants.low: Legion soldiers on the border road. Recalled two centuries ago. We're what's left of them.
variants.high: The column was Legion soldiers set to hold the border road. The order to leave came about two centuries back. We keep their duty roster and wear their colours. I'm proud of that much.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Gideon is the frontier city, out west. It's the first settlement you reach on the Blackwood Road coming down from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit and hear cases. That matters for an Owing, which is a debt worked off in labour. An Owing made in Gideon is a paper contract. A court can contest it.

variants.low: The frontier city in the west, first on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit. An Owing made there is paper, so a court can contest it.
variants.high: Gideon is the frontier city, out west. It's the first settlement on the Blackwood Road coming down from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit. An Owing made there is a paper contract, so a court can contest it. If you're bound to one, that road is worth walking. Leyawiin trade keeps us fed when the road is open.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Levy's due below.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: One traveller. Levy's entered.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: It's two watches since the last traveller.

variants.low: I'm on watch. Keep walking.
variants.high: It's two watches since a traveller, sir. Come up.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: It's quiet. Try the fire.

variants.low: Quiet. Leave me be.
variants.high: It's quiet, sir. Try the fire.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: You are the thief. The serjeant will hear.

variants.low: Touch it and the serjeant wakes.
variants.high: Hands off that, friend! Serjeant will hear.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: It's you again. The sky's been quiet.

variants.low: Here once more. Levy first.
variants.high: You again, sir. The sky's been quiet.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: Four tents on a bench above the Mile House track. I stand a watch here, that's all. The tarn's at our back.

variants.low: Four tents on the bench above the Mile House track. Nothing here for you.
variants.high: Four tents on a bench above the Mile House track. Take the fire if you're cold, sir. The tarn's at our back.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: I stand the watch. It's called on the hour, day and night. Mine is the day watch, on the uphill side.

variants.low: We stand the watch. It's called on the hour. That's the work.
variants.high: I stand the watch. It's called on the hour, day and night. Mine is the day, uphill. It's honest work, sir.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: The serjeant writes the duty roster himself, in his own hand. Six names on it, mine too. They're sound men. Every one stands his watch.

variants.low: The serjeant keeps the roster in his own hand. Six names. Ask him.
variants.high: The serjeant writes the roster in his own hand. Six names, mine too. They're sound men, sir. Every one stands his watch.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: Wings in the nests on the hill above. I stand the day watch right under them. The rats come at night, down from the marsh.

variants.low: Wings in the nests uphill. Rats at night. Keep clear of both.
variants.high: Wings in the nests on the hill above. I stand under them by day. Rats at night. Keep to the track, sir.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: Go down the track. You reach the Mile House first, the one with the eagle. Cartwright's Cross lies further along the road.

variants.low: Down the track. The Mile House, then Cartwright's Cross. Go.
variants.high: Down the track, sir. The Mile House with the eagle comes first. Cartwright's Cross lies further along the road. Mind the ruts.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: Soldiers of the Legion, posted on the border road. Command recalled them about two centuries ago. We kept the colours. That's the whole of it.

variants.low: Legion soldiers on the border road. Recalled two centuries gone. That's all.
variants.high: Soldiers of the Legion, posted on the border road. Command recalled them two centuries back. We kept the colours, sir.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. So is the Mile House, a waystation. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.

variants.low: Old Imperial roads, the Prison road and the Border road. Folk keep the old names. A Tag House on a dry rise beside the first.
variants.high: Old Imperial roads, sir, the Prison road and the Border road, with the Mile House as a waystation. Folk keep the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: Gideon is the frontier city in the west. Coming from Cyrodiil by the Blackwood Road, it's the first town you meet. The courts there still work. An Owing made there is only paper, so you can fight it before a judge.

variants.low: Gideon is the frontier city in the west. First town on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Its courts still work. An Owing there is paper you can contest.
variants.high: Gideon is the frontier city in the west, sir. Coming from Cyrodiil by the Blackwood Road, it's the first town you meet. The courts still work. An Owing made there is only paper, so you can fight it before a judge.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: It's half a watch.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: I've seen no wings.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Stop there, citizen. I'm cooking.

variants.low: Not now, citizen. I've a pot to mind.
variants.high: Come to the fire, citizen. Mind the pot.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: The fire's banked. Breakfast is barley.

variants.low: Fire's banked. Go away till morning.
variants.high: The fire's banked, but there's barley going.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Leave that sack. It's tomorrow's supper.

variants.low: Put it down, or I fetch the serjeant.
variants.high: Leave that sack, friend. I'll share it out.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Back so soon, citizen? The levy's still due.

variants.low: Levy first, citizen. The pot won't wait.
variants.high: Sit, citizen. The pot's warm.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: This is a posting on a level bench by a spring tarn, up in the hills where the Gideon road can't see it. I cook at the fire by the command tent. Six of us are on the roster now. The pot has to stretch to all of us.

variants.low: It's a camp on a bench. Ask the serjeant if you want more. I've a pot to mind.
variants.high: It's a posting on a level bench by a spring tarn, up where the Gideon road can't see it. I cook here for the watch. Sit by the fire if your feet are tired. The pot's thin, but it's hot.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: I'm the cook for the watch, so I make what the levy buys. It buys less barley every season. A man who pays at the barricade stays a traveller until the camp has fed him. I keep a ladle spare for that.

variants.low: I cook. A man stays a traveller until the camp has fed him. That's how it is here.
variants.high: I cook for the watch with whatever the levy buys. That's less barley every season. A man who pays at the barricade stays a traveller until the camp has fed him. For you I'll find a ladle.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Six are on the roster. Every one of them stands a watch, me included. Severa and Anwen eat at my fire. Gnaeus Martius is the serjeant. He writes the roster in his own hand.

variants.low: Six on the roster. Every one stands a watch. The serjeant keeps the roster.
variants.high: Six are on the roster. Every man stands a watch. Severa and Anwen eat at my fire. Gnaeus Martius is the serjeant. He writes the roster himself, in his own hand. The names are all in there.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Hackwings nest on the hill over the tents, but they keep to the hill. The rats are the trouble. They get into the meal sacks at night, so I stack the sacks myself.

variants.low: Hackwings on the hill. Rats in the sacks. Keep off the hill.
variants.high: Hackwings nest on the hill over the tents, but they keep to the hill. The rats get into the meal sacks at night. I stack the sacks myself, so you'll not be bitten by anything here if you stay by the fire.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Take the track north-west from the barricade to the Mile House, a few minutes' walk. For Cartwright's Cross it's longer: east, then south-west, then north-west, then west along the Blackwood Road, then north-west again. Each leg is a few minutes. After the Cross you're on the Gideon road.

variants.low: North-west to the Mile House, a few minutes. The Cross is further. Follow the turnings.
variants.high: North-west along the track from the barricade brings you to the Mile House in a few minutes. For Cartwright's Cross, go east, then south-west, then north-west, then west on the Blackwood Road, then north-west again. Each leg is a few minutes. After the Cross you're on the Gideon road.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: The column was Legion soldiers posted along this frontier. About two centuries back, the Legion called them home with their wages still owing. Part of them stayed on here instead of marching out. The pay never came. The last entry in the pay book is theirs. The men on the roster are their sons and grandsons.

variants.low: The Legion was recalled about two centuries back with our wages owing. Part of the column stayed. The pay never came.
variants.high: The column was Legion soldiers posted along this frontier. When the Legion was recalled, their pay was owing. Part of them stayed on here. The pay never came. The last entry in the pay book is theirs. The men on the roster are their sons and grandsons.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Mind the fire.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: More water now.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Chasepoint is a stage on the coast road. The Legion built it. Wreck-salvage families keep it now. Salvage rights pass from parent to child. Rope is dried in the old stable. Two of the families each claim to be keeper there.

variants.low: A coast road stage the Legion built. Salvage families keep it. Rights pass down. Two families claim the keeper's post.
variants.high: Chasepoint is a stage on the coast road, put up by the Legion. Wreck-salvage families keep it now. Their rights pass from parent to child. They dry rope in the old stable. Two families each claim to be keeper there.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Page forty of the pay book shows the arrears, so a pardon alone is no use to me. The Mile House talks of a pardon and a wage from Gideon. They add that the governor refuses to pay for clearing us. The toll company would rather hire the men than buy them off.

variants.low: A pardon without the arrears in the pay book is worth nothing. The Mile House talks of Gideon, a pardon, a wage. The governor refuses to clear us. The toll company would rather hire the men.
variants.high: Page forty of the pay book shows the arrears, so a pardon alone is no use to me. The Mile House talks of a pardon and a wage from Gideon. They add that the governor refuses to pay for clearing us. The toll company would rather hire the men than buy them off. Bring me word if it is true.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: We are the remains of a Legion column. The recall came and the men were never paid. Their sons and grandsons live on the shelf above the Mile House track. I am one of them.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: Blackwood is hill country in the west of the province. A road climbs through it into Cyrodiil. The hill people stay by their own tree's roots. They care little for strangers. A riddle they will always take.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
entries.words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House was a waystation on them. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A dry rise carries the Tag House beside it.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: Blackwood is the hill country, out west in Black Marsh. The road up to Cyrodiil climbs through it. Hill folk keep to the roots of their own tree and show strangers little interest. They like a riddle.

variants.low: Hill country in the west of the marsh. The Cyrodiil road climbs through it. They like riddles. Leave them be.
variants.high: Blackwood is the hill country, out west in Black Marsh. The road up to Cyrodiil climbs through it. Hill folk keep to the roots of their own tree. They like a riddle, sir, if you have one.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
entries.words: It's what's left of a Legion column. Once recalled, the Legion never paid them a coin. The sons and grandsons of those men live in the camp on the bench above the Mile House track.

variants.low: What's left of a Legion column. The Legion never paid them. Their sons and grandsons live on this bench.
variants.high: It's what's left of a Legion column, sir. Once recalled, the Legion never paid them a coin. The sons and grandsons of those men live in the camp on this bench.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: Blackwood is hilly ground along the western edge of the province. The Blackwood Road climbs up through those hills into Cyrodiil. I only know the hill people from the road folk who pass my fire. They keep close to their own tree and show strangers little curiosity, but they like a riddle.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: That's us. We're what's left of a Legion column. The Legion never paid these men when it was recalled. Their sons and grandsons live here now, in a camp on a shelf of level ground up the hill from the Mile House track. I feed them.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
entries.words: The Imperials laid those roads. The Mile House was their waystation. People still use the old names, Border road and Prison road. The Prison road heads off to the Rose. You'll find the Tag House on a dry rise by that road.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Blackwood's the hill country across the western side of Black Marsh. The road named for it climbs those hills up to Cyrodiil. The hill people stay near the roots of their own tree and don't care to talk to strangers. They do love a riddle, I'm told. I can't say I've had one out of them.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: That's us, the leavings of a Legion column. The men were owed their pay when the Legion marched home. It never came. Their sons and grandsons hold the colours still, in a camp on this bench above the Mile House track. The book calls it a post.

entries.speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
entries.words: Those are old Imperial roads, with the Mile House as a waystation on them. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads toward a place called the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.
